# `⟜` — After

`f⟜g Y` is `Y f(g Y)`: `g` prepares the right argument of `f`, and `f` still gets `Y` on the left. For `f(g Y)`, use [Atop](rank.qmd), `f⍤g`.

```apl
×⟜- 5              ⍝ ¯25
```

`X f⟜g Y` is `X f(g Y)`.

```apl
10 +⟜- 3           ⍝ 7
"abc" ,⟜⌽ "de"     ⍝ "abced"
```

`f⟜A` binds the right argument. The bound function takes one argument. A literal argument straight after a literal operand joins its strand: `-⟜10 3` binds the vector `10 3` and has no argument. Put the function in parentheses, as in `(-⟜10) 3`, or use a name.

```apl
(-⟜10)3            ⍝ ¯7
y←3 ⋄ -⟜10 y       ⍝ ¯7
```

See [Before](before.qmd), [Atop / Rank](rank.qmd) and [Over](over.qmd).
